rows.grounds: the seed-syllable vāgbhava (origin-of-speech bīja), object of utterance
sandhi fusion of bījam (seed) and uccāryam (to-be-uttered); gerundive qualifying the seed
compound: jīva (life) + prāṇa (vital-breath) + samanvita (endowed-with), qualifying the seed

items.question: Which seed-syllable, endowed with life and vital breath, must be uttered in this practice?
premises: The vāgbhava seed-syllable is specified as the object of utterance.
This seed-syllable is designated as something to be uttered.
The utterance must be accompanied by life and vital breath.
items.inference: Therefore, the practitioner must utter the vāgbhava bīja while it is conjoined with jīva and prāṇa.
uncertainties: The precise technical sense of jīva and prāṇa in this Śrīvidyā context (literal breath, subtle vital forces, or mantra-internal features) is not fully specified in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: One should utter the vāgbhava seed-syllable, endowed with life and vital breath.
